THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

High-Protein Viral Dot Cake

Viral dot cake, protein version. 3 ramekin cakes per batch, 250 cal / 25g protein each (base 170/19 + cheesecake frosting + sprinkles).

YIELD3 servings
TOTAL TIME25 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~250 cal | ~25g protein

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 2 scoops (62g) PEScience Select Gourmet Vanilla Protein Powder
  • 3 large Happy Egg Co Organic Free-Range Eggs
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) Fairlife Fat-Free Ultra-Filtered Milk
  • 45g all-purpose flour
  • 15g Whole Earth Monk Fruit Erythritol Sweetener Blend
  • 15g Jell-O Sugar-Free Vanilla Instant Pudding Mix (about half a 1 oz box)

Ingredients — continued

  • 1 tsp Clabber Girl Double-Acting Baking Powder
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • Cooking spray (for ramekins)
  • 1 serving (30g) Protein Cheesecake Frosting per cake — 60 cal / 6g protein each
  • Rainbow nonpareil sprinkles, ~5g per cake (~20 cal/cake)

You saw the viral dot cake on TikTok and want the protein version. 3 ramekin cakes per batch, 250 cal / 25g protein each finished. Bake the bases (15 min) → chill → top with one 30g serving of [Protein Cheesecake Frosting](/cookbook/protein-cheesecake-frosting) per cake → press into rainbow nonpareils. The frosted top + sprinkle coat is the visual hook; the liquidy center is the texture payoff.

Method

  1. 1.PREHEAT. Oven to 350°F. Spray 3 ramekins (6-8 oz size) with cooking spray.
  2. 2.DRY MIX. In a mixing bowl on a scale, combine 62g PEScience Vanilla + 45g AP flour + 15g Whole Earth Monk Fruit Erythritol + 15g Jell-O Sugar-Free Vanilla Pudding Mix + 1 tsp Clabber Girl baking powder. Whisk dry to break up any protein-powder clumps.
  3. 3.WET MIX. In a separate bowl, whisk 3 eggs + 1/4 cup Fairlife + 1 tsp vanilla extract until uniform.
  4. 4.COMBINE. Pour the wet into the dry. Whisk until smooth — should be thick cake batter that just barely flows off the whisk. Don't overmix; lumps cook out.
  5. 5.FILL RAMEKINS. Divide batter evenly across 3 ramekins. Smooth the tops with a spatula. Ramekins should be ~3/4 full — the cakes rise then settle.
  6. 6.BAKE 350°F × 15 MIN. Tops should be golden + spring back lightly. Centers should still feel SOFT to the touch — the liquidy-molten center is the viral dot cake signature. Past 18 min = dry center = lost moment.
  7. 7.COOL + TRIM. Let ramekins cool 10 min on a wire rack, then chill in the fridge 30 min (or overnight). Once chilled, slice the domed top off each cake with a serrated knife so the surface is flat for frosting. The trimmed scraps = the 4th serving (snack them, freeze for parfaits, or compost).
  8. 8.FROST. Spread one 30g serving of [Protein Cheesecake Frosting](/cookbook/protein-cheesecake-frosting) over each flat-trimmed cake top. Smooth to the edges. Thick frosting holds peaks; thin frosting pools — refer to the parent frosting recipe troubleshooting if it's too thin.
  9. 9.SPRINKLE DIP. Pour ~5g rainbow nonpareils onto a shallow plate. Press the frosted top of each cake into the sprinkles to coat. Lift gently — frosting holds the sprinkles in place.
  10. 10.SCOOP + EAT. Best within 2 hours of frosting (sprinkle crunch fades after 4-6 hours as moisture migrates). Scoop through the sprinkle top + frosting + cake — molten center reveals itself on the spoon.

If something fails

Center came out fully baked / not liquidy: Overbaked. 15 min @ 350°F is the floor — if your oven runs hot, drop to 13 min. The center is SUPPOSED to be soft/molten — that's the viral dot cake signature. Once a center fully sets, you can't un-set it.

Batter overflowed the ramekins: You used smaller ramekins (4 oz instead of 6-8 oz). The recipe yields enough batter for 3 standard 6-8 oz ramekins. With smaller ramekins, divide across 4 — or trim the rims more aggressively after baking.

Cake collapsed after pulling from oven: Slight collapse is fine — the center moisture pulls the top down a bit. Excessive collapse = underbaked. Add 2-3 min next time + check again at 13 min.

Frosting won't stick / slides off: Cakes weren't fully chilled before frosting. The frosting needs cold cake to grip. Chill another 15-20 min then frost. Or thicken the frosting — see the parent recipe troubleshooting.

Sprinkles fall off / won't coat: Frosting layer is too thin. Use the full 30g per cake (not less). Press the frosted top INTO the sprinkles with light pressure — don't sprinkle on top, that doesn't bond.

Macros came in higher than 250 cal / cake: Most likely cause: (1) heavier sprinkle dose (>5g per cake adds ~5 cal per extra gram), (2) larger frosting portion (40g instead of 30g = +20 cal). The 250 / 25 anchor assumes 1 trimmed cake + 30g frosting + 5g sprinkles. Stick to those weights.

Storage and reheating

Store: Bake the cakes ahead, chill un-frosted up to 3 days in airtight container. Frost + sprinkle right before serving — sprinkles lose their crunch within 4-6 hours of contact with frosting moisture.

Reheat: Don't reheat frosted cakes (frosting breaks). For unfrosted: microwave 10-15 sec to soften the center back to liquidy if eaten cold. Best at chilled-to-room-temp.

Lasts: Un-frosted cakes: 3 days refrigerated, 1 month frozen. Frosted + sprinkled cakes: best within 2 hours; OK overnight but sprinkles soften. Trimmed-top scraps: 2-3 days in airtight container as a snack.

Per finished cake (~250 cal / 25g protein) MacroFactor-tracked. Component breakdown per cake: base cake portion ~170 cal / 19g protein + 30g Protein Cheesecake Frosting ~60 cal / 6g protein + ~5g rainbow nonpareils ~20 cal / 0g protein = 250 cal / 25g protein per cake. Batter math (yields 4 servings of base cake, 3 of which are frosted into finished cakes; the 4th is the trimmed-top scrap from the 3 ramekins): 62g PEScience (~220 cal / 48P) + 3 eggs (~210 cal / 18P) + 1/4 cup Fairlife (~22 cal / 2P) + 45g AP flour (~165 cal / 5P) + 15g Whole Earth (~0 cal) + 15g Jell-O SF Pudding (~25 cal / 0P) + 1 tsp baking powder + 1 tsp vanilla ≈ 642 cal / 73P batter total ÷ 4 servings = 160 cal / 18.3P per base-cake serving. Per Tushar's MacroFactor log this rounds to 170 / 19. Flagged estimated because (1) flour brand varies cal slightly, (2) sprinkle dose is eyeballed, (3) cheesecake frosting macros are themselves estimated (see parent recipe). The 250 / 25 anchor holds for 1 trimmed cake + 30g frosting + 5g sprinkles.

Core ratio — locked

62g PEScience Select Gourmet Vanilla (2 scoops) + 3 large eggs + 1/4 cup Fairlife Fat-Free + 45g AP flour + 15g Whole Earth Monk Fruit Erythritol + 15g Jell-O Sugar-Free Vanilla Pudding Mix + 1 tsp Clabber Girl baking powder + 1 tsp vanilla extract. Yields batter for 4 servings (170 cal / 19g protein each); divided into 3 ramekins with the tops trimmed flat after baking — the trimmed scraps = the 4th serving (snack on its own or add to a parfait, ~170 cal / 19g protein unfrosted).

Flavor target

Cake center should be **liquidy-soft, not set** (the 15-min bake is intentionally short — viral dot cake is supposed to have a molten center). Top should be lightly golden, smooth enough to hold a flat frosting layer. Frosting + sprinkle coat reads like funfetti birthday cake. Don't overbake — past 18 min the center dries out and you lose the moment.

Brands I use

PEScience
Select Gourmet Vanilla Protein (24g protein per 31g scoop — 2 scoops / 62g per batter)
Whey + casein blend that bakes into actual cake texture (not the gritty/rubber result you get from straight whey isolate when heated). Gourmet Vanilla is the smooth-vanilla flavor lane — NOT the Cake Pop flavor (too sweet on top of pudding mix + monk fruit). Cross-recipe with the Protein Cheesecake Frosting + Chocolate Protein Brownie Bowl + Mocha Brownie Creami.
Happy Egg Co.
Organic Free-Range Large Brown Eggs, dozen carton (~70 cal / 6g protein per large egg — 3 eggs per batch)
Pastured + USDA Organic — rich orange yolks. The yolk fat is what gives the cake the soft custard-like center that holds the molten texture at 15 min. Sub any large eggs; the protein math holds regardless of farm.
Fairlife
Fat-Free Ultra-Filtered Milk, 1/4 cup (~22 cal / 2g protein per 1/4 cup)
Lactose-free + 50% more protein than regular milk. Small amount in the batter for hydration + protein bump. Cross-recipe staple across the cookbook (cereal hack, cheesecake frosting, muffin cup powerup).
Whole Earth
Monk Fruit with Erythritol Sweetener Blend (15g per batter)
1:1 sugar substitute. 0 cal, zero glycemic. The sweetener that keeps the cake at 170 cal / serving without losing the dessert flavor. Sub Lakanto, Swerve, or any monk-fruit-erythritol blend.
Jell-O
Sugar-Free Vanilla Instant Pudding Mix, 1 oz box (15g per batter = half a box)
Locks in the vanilla cake flavor + helps the cake set without adding sugar. Cross-recipe with the Protein Cheesecake Frosting (uses the cheesecake variant). The Vanilla pudding mix + monk fruit combo is what makes a protein cake taste like cake, not a protein bar.
Clabber Girl
Double-Acting Baking Powder, 8.1 oz can (1 tsp per batter — gluten-free, no aluminum)
Standard baking-powder leavening. Double-acting = activates twice (once when wet, once when heated) for consistent rise. Sub any gluten-free baking powder.
Protein Cheesecake Frosting
Parent recipe — 60 cal / 6g protein per 30g serving, makes 15 servings per batch
The frosting topping. Make a batch via the parent recipe and you have enough for ~5 batches of dot cakes (15 servings ÷ 3 cakes per batch). Cross-recipe link is the whole architecture here — both recipes share the PEScience + Jell-O + Whole Earth brand stack.
